official.deadline_note: The KMSP deadline is the later of two gates: the UW-Madison Early Action application is due November 1, 2026 with all application materials due November 9, 2026. Only candidates admitted to UW-Madison in the Early Action review period are eligible for the scholarship, and no late applications are accepted for any reason - no deadline extensions are offered.
official.application_cycle: Cohort 11, beginning studies at UW-Madison in Fall 2027; the WiSH scholarship application opened by late August 2026 and scholarship decisions are released by the end of March.
official.status_note: Live cycle: kmsp.wisc.edu lists 'APPLY HERE! Due: November 1, 2026' for UW-Madison International Admissions and 'APPLY HERE! Due: November 15, 2026' for the WiSH KMSP application portal, and the WiSH opportunity 106724 shows a deadline of 11/15/2026 for Cohort 11 (Fall 2027 entry).
official.tuition_coverage_note: WiSH lists the award as 'Full Tuition, Room & Board'. kmsp.wisc.edu and admissions.wisc.edu state that scholars 'receive a full time, four-year/eight-semester scholarship to the University of Wisconsin-Madison that includes tuition and fees, on campus room and board, health insurance, airfare, and a stipend for miscellaneous expenses.' The Program Support page adds that financial support covers 'payment of tuition and fees, university housing, and SHIP premiums' plus 'stipend payments for basic living expenses and expenses for scholars living off-campus.'
benefits: A stipend for miscellaneous expenses (stipend payments for basic living expenses and expenses for scholars living off-campus)
Travel booking support for annual trip home and bringing family members to Madison, WI for graduation
eligibility: Be an incoming first-year, undergraduate, bachelor's degree-seeking student with no prior tertiary education at another institution
Apply to UW-Madison Early Action and receive an admit decision in the Early Action review period
Demonstrate a high level of financial need
Demonstrate a commitment to poverty alleviation and community development
Plan to return to their home country/region after graduation

Earn a high school diploma or equivalent credential that meets UW-Madison admission requirements for first-year entry from an institution in Africa, the Caribbean, Latin America, South Asia, or Southeast Asia (received on or after November 1, 2023, or in the final year of study with expected completion before August 1, 2027)
requirements: Maintain a minimum 3.0 grade point average (GPA)
Complete at least 12 credits as a full-time student each semester

Actively participate in program activities including individual advising appointments, program meetings, and other scheduled programming; respond to KMSP communications in a timely manner and submit absence requests to the program manager in advance
Participate in Orientation and the Wisconsin Experience Seminar during the first fall semester
Follow all university policies and state/federal laws and be a good citizen of the general University community
Agree to these terms at acceptance of the scholarship; expectations may be adjusted at the discretion of KMSP staff with clear rationale and advance notice
documents: UW-Madison undergraduate application (Common Application or Universities of Wisconsin Application) submitted under Early Action
Non-refundable $80 application fee, or an application fee waiver request
Two essays: a personal essay and a 'why UW-Madison / why this major' response
Course and grade information for grades 9-12 plus the official country-specific secondary credential for attainment of the diploma
One required letter of recommendation from a teacher, school counselor, or faculty member
WiSH King-Morgridge Scholars Program application: acknowledgement questions, short-answer eligibility questions and one 500-700 word essay
selection_criteria: Holistic review taking into account school and community involvement, essays, the connection between degree interests and professional aims, commitment to poverty alleviation and community development, and first generation status
Selected for their drive, academic success and commitment to addressing problems of poverty in their own countries
Six students are admitted to the program annually
Selection is made by the UW-Madison Office of Admissions and Recruitment together with KMSP staff
coverage: Full Tuition, Room & Board (WiSH award line)
On campus room and board (university housing)
Stipend for miscellaneous expenses and basic living expenses
application_method: Submit the UW-Madison undergraduate application and all required application materials by the Early Action deadlines (application November 1; materials November 9)
Set up your NetID using the UW-Madison Campus ID number sent via email in the application confirmation
Log in to the WiSH portal using your NetID and password
Answer a series of multiple-choice questions, which will create your opportunities list in WiSH
Complete the King-Morgridge Scholars Program application, consisting of several short-answer questions to determine eligibility as well as a 500-700 word essay, by November 15
official.application_route: Two-stage: first be admitted to UW-Madison through Early Action (application due November 1, materials November 9), then complete the separate KMSP application in the Wisconsin Scholarship Hub (WiSH) by November 15 using your NetID.
official.citizenship_residency: No citizenship test is published. Eligibility rests on where the secondary credential was earned - from an institution in one of the listed eligible countries in Africa, the Caribbean, Latin America, South Asia, or Southeast Asia - and applicants must plan to return to their home country/region after graduation.
official.international_eligibility: Yes. The programme is administered by UW-Madison's International Division and is designed for students educated outside the United States in the listed regions. UW-Madison states it does not partner with third-party agents or educational consultants to represent the university or recruit international students.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No subject or field restriction is published for KMSP; applicants name a first and second choice major on the admission application, and direct entry to business, engineering, dance or music carries different admissions expectations.
official.description: The King-Morgridge Scholars Program (KMSP) is a four-year, full-tuition scholarship for enterprising, creative, dedicated students committed to applying their talents toward poverty alleviation around the globe. Made possible through generous gifts by the King and Morgridge families, it is housed in UW-Madison's International Division and provides six scholarships per year to students from Africa, the Caribbean, Latin America, South Asia, and Southeast Asia who are selected for their drive, academic success, and commitment to addressing problems of poverty in their own countries.
official.program_type: Donor-endowed four-year full-tuition scholarship for international first-year undergraduates, University of Wisconsin-Madison International Division
official.english_requirement: First-year applicants educated in non-English speaking countries must submit an official TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo English Test (DET) score, unless English was the primary language of instruction in all four years of secondary school. Published minimums: DET 115+, IELTS 6.5+, TOEFL iBT 80 (test date on or before 1/20/26) or 4.5 (test date 1/21/26 or later). Scores must be sent electronically directly from the testing service, cannot be older than two years, and are not superscored. IB HL English, AP English, ACT, SAT, Cambridge English Exam and PTE scores cannot be used to waive the requirement. Sending scores adds 1-6 weeks to application completion.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a six-place, everything-paid package aimed squarely at first-generation students from the eligible regions who could not otherwise afford a U.S. degree: tuition and fees, on-campus room and board, health insurance, airfare and a living stipend for four years. Because only six scholars are chosen each year and you must already be admitted to UW-Madison, the date to work back from is November 1 for the admission application and November 9 for its materials, with November 15 reserved for the KMSP essay in WiSH. UW-Madison publishes no dollar value, so plan against the university's own cost of attendance and set aside money for the $80 application fee, English test fees and score delivery, visa costs, books and personal travel.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A first-generation, financially needy applicant from an eligible African, Caribbean, Latin American, South Asian or Southeast Asian country who has just finished or is finishing secondary school and can name one concrete development problem at home they intend to work on.
application_readiness_checklist: Sit TOEFL, IELTS or DET no later than September so electronic scores (TOEFL code 1846) reach UW-Madison before the November 9 materials deadline; there is no superscoring and scores must be under two years old.
Ask a teacher or counselor for the single required letter of recommendation in early September and confirm they will submit it directly from the school.

Assemble the country-specific credential set (attested board results certificates, WASSCE results, KCSE, UACE and similar) rather than relying on a school transcript - results listed on transcripts are not accepted.
If English was your language of instruction for all four secondary years, file the ELP Waiver eForm in Student Center early; the office allows 14 business days after the transcript arrives.

Build the 500-700 word essay around one named poverty, economic or community development challenge in your own country and how a UW-Madison degree equips you to address it; keep any AI use to brainstorming or proofreading.
Attend a free virtual information session and email kmscholars@admissions.wisc.edu with anything ambiguous well before mid-November.
common_rejection_risks: Treating November 15 as the only deadline: the scholarship is never reviewed if the admission file is still incomplete at the November 9 materials deadline.
Being deferred in the Early Action round - only Early Action admits are eligible, and a defer pushes the decision to the end of March, after the six places are filled.
Any prior tertiary education, even one completed semester or a finished post-secondary diploma, makes an applicant ineligible outright.
A secondary credential earned before November 1, 2023 or one that will not be completed before August 1, 2027, which puts the applicant outside the window.
Documents that arrive late or unverifiably: a paper-mailed transcript, a WASSCE result with no scratch card verification, or an English translation sent by email instead of an official route.
An essay that reads as AI-drafted or ghost-written, or that discusses poverty generically without being anchored in the applicant's own country and region.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The award covers tuition and fees, university housing, health insurance, airfare and a stipend for basic living expenses, but no stipend amount is published, so applicants should still budget for the non-refundable $80 application fee (waivable), TOEFL/IELTS/DET fees and score delivery, visa and SEVIS costs, books and course supplies, personal extras, and any cost of living off campus beyond what the stipend covers.
document_audit: Country-specific credentials outrank transcripts: attested copies of the actual board-issued results certificates are required for Indian, Pakistani, Bangladeshi, West African (WASSCE), Kenyan, Ugandan and similar curricula.
WASSCE applicants must complete the Scratch Card E-Form in Student Center so UW-Madison can verify results online.
If your school does not issue English transcripts, the official translation must come from the school or an EducationUSA official and be sent through an official channel - email is not accepted.
The letter of recommendation must come from the recommender, carry your full name and birth date, and expires one year after it is written.
The $80 application fee is non-refundable; request the waiver inside the application at submission rather than afterwards.
English scores must be sent electronically by the testing service - paper IELTS copies are refused, and the DET must be sent to 'University of Wisconsin-Madison' under Undergraduate with sub-scores.
alerts: Two deadlines, one gate: November 1 for the UW-Madison application and November 9 for materials, then November 15 for the KMSP essay. The programme states that no late applications are accepted for any reason and that no deadline extensions are possible.
You must be admitted in the Early Action review to receive the award, so a defer or deny decision ends your KMSP candidacy for that cycle.
The WiSH application needs a NetID built from the Campus ID emailed in your application confirmation - do not leave that handoff to the last days before November 15.
The award is conditional on a 3.0 GPA and at least 12 credits each semester, and scholars agree to these terms on acceptance; unmet expectations can terminate the scholarship.
Eligibility includes planning to return to your home country or region after graduation, which matters if you later intend to build a career in the United States.
Six awards per year are spread across roughly 100 eligible countries, so the essays and the financial-need answers are the real differentiators, not grades alone.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the admission application under Early Action, wait for the Campus ID email to create your NetID, then complete the KMSP application in the Wisconsin Scholarship Hub - the scholarship is only considered once the Early Action admission decision lands.
